FEEDBACK: The second SPARQL constraint only requires each upper-waterline point to equal some intended-waterline point; it does not ensure that point is the highest intended point at that longitudinal position. Thus an upper line containing both a lower intended point and the true maximum can pass. Repair it so each upper point must coincide with an intended point at the same longitudinal position and vertical coordinate and must fail if any intended point at that position has a greater vertical coordinate. Retain the first constraint to ensure every intended longitudinal position is represented by an upper point that is not lower.

Prevent ambiguous and accidental-pass representations: require exactly one upper ice waterline with sh:maxCount 1; require exactly one longitudinalPosition and verticalCoordinate per profile point; and require exactly one qudt:numericValue and one qudt:unit per QuantityValue. The current sh:hasValue unit:M still permits additional conflicting units, and unrestricted multiplicities create Cartesian-product comparisons that can pass without a uniquely defined coordinate or UIWL.
